title: Policies and processes
text: Policies, processes, procedures and practices for mapping, measuring and managing AI risk exist, are transparent and are applied; legal and regulatory requirements are understood; risk tolerance is defined; documentation, inventory and decommissioning are covered.

title: Accountability structures
text: Clear accountability so teams and individuals are empowered, responsible and trained to manage AI risk; roles, leadership engagement and oversight responsibilities are documented.

title: Diverse and inclusive workforce
text: Workforce diversity, equity, inclusion and accessibility are prioritised in mapping, measuring and managing AI risk; humans oversee the AI system with defined roles.

title: Risk-aware culture
text: Teams are committed to a culture that considers and communicates AI risk, practises critical thinking and a safety-first mindset, documents risks and impacts, and shares lessons learned.

title: Stakeholder engagement
text: Robust engagement with relevant AI actors and affected communities; feedback from users and the public is collected, considered and integrated into the system.

title: Third-party and supply chain
text: Policies address risks and benefits of third-party software, models and data and other supply chain issues, including contingency plans for failures of third-party components.

title: Context established
text: Intended purpose, users, laws, norms, deployment setting and assumptions are established and understood; interdisciplinary input is gathered; decisions about whether to build or deploy are made with risk tolerance in view.

title: System categorisation
text: The AI system is categorised by tasks and methods; knowledge limits and how human oversight is used are documented, and scientific integrity and test-set practices are considered.

title: Capabilities, usage and costs
text: Capabilities, targeted usage, goals, expected benefits and costs compared with benchmarks are understood; operator and practitioner proficiency and human-AI oversight are defined.

title: Component risks and benefits
text: Risks and benefits are mapped for all components of the AI system including third-party software and data; legal risks such as intellectual property and privacy are identified and internal controls assessed.

title: Impact characterisation
text: Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact on individuals, groups, communities, organisations and society are characterised, including harms from misuse and beneficial and negative outcomes.

title: Methods and metrics
text: Appropriate methods and metrics for AI risks are identified and applied; their appropriateness is regularly assessed, and independent experts or users take part in assessment.

title: Trustworthiness evaluation
text: AI systems are evaluated for trustworthy characteristics: testing on representative data, validity and reliability, safety, security and resilience, transparency, explainability, privacy risk and fairness with harmful bias examined.

title: Risk tracking over time
text: Mechanisms for tracking identified AI risks over time are in place, including hard-to-assess or emergent risks and the input of domain experts and users.

title: Measurement feedback
text: Feedback on how effective the measurement is gets gathered and assessed, including reports from end users and the consistency of results with deployment context.

title: Prioritise and respond to risks
text: Risks from MAP and MEASURE are prioritised, responded to and managed; decide whether the system meets its purpose, treat high-priority risks by mitigating, transferring, avoiding or accepting them.

title: Maximise benefit, minimise harm
text: Strategies to maximise benefits and minimise negative impacts are planned, documented and informed by relevant AI actors; mechanisms exist to supersede, disengage or deactivate systems with unexpected outcomes.

title: Third-party risk management
text: AI risks and benefits from third-party entities are managed; pre-trained models and third-party data are monitored and risk controls applied.

title: Treatment, response and communication
text: Risk treatments including response, recovery and communication plans are documented and monitored regularly; post-deployment monitoring, incident reporting, appeals and updates are in place.

title: Valid and reliable
text: The system performs accurately and consistently as intended over time and across conditions; errors, drift and poor generalisation are measured and monitored.

title: Safe
text: The system does not endanger human life, health, property or the environment under defined conditions; real-time monitoring and the ability to shut down are provided.

title: Secure and resilient
text: The system withstands adversarial attacks, data poisoning, model theft and unexpected events, and maintains confidentiality, integrity and availability.

title: Accountable and transparent
text: Information about the system and its outputs is available to the people who use it; documentation, disclosure and responsibility for outcomes are clear.

title: Explainable and interpretable
text: Users can understand how the system works and why it produced an output, in terms suited to their role and context.

title: Privacy-enhanced
text: Human autonomy, identity and dignity are protected through data minimisation, consent, anonymisation, access control and limiting leakage of personal data.

title: Fair with harmful bias managed
text: Systemic, computational and human-cognitive bias are identified and managed; outcomes are equitable across demographic groups and accessibility is considered.

title: Confabulation
text: Generative models can confidently produce false or fabricated content, such as invented facts, citations or advice, which users may rely on.

title: Dangerous, violent or hateful content
text: Generative systems may be induced to produce content that eases access to harmful capabilities or that is violent, hateful or incites self-harm.

title: Data privacy
text: Models can leak, memorise or infer personal data from training data or prompts, and input data may be retained or reused without consent.

title: Human-AI configuration
text: Over-reliance on or automation bias toward generated output, anthropomorphism and poor handoff between people and the system lead to errors.

title: Information integrity
text: Generated text, images or audio can scale misinformation, disinformation and synthetic media, making it harder to tell what is authentic.

title: Information security
text: Prompt injection, jailbreaks, data poisoning and unauthorised access can compromise generative systems and the data and tools connected to them.

title: Intellectual property
text: Generated content may reproduce copyrighted, trademarked or licensed material, and training data may be used without permission.

title: Harmful bias and homogenisation
text: Outputs can reflect and amplify stereotypes and narrow or homogenised content, and performance can differ across languages and groups.

title: Value chain and component integration
text: Reliance on third-party models, datasets, APIs and open-source components with unclear provenance creates opaque risk that is hard to audit.

title: Environmental impacts
text: Training and serving large models consumes significant energy, compute and water, with carbon and resource costs.
